evals.name: onboard-to-refunds-repo
evals.prompt: I'm new on the refunds team. Can you walk me through how this repo works? Mostly I want to understand what happens when a support agent creates a refund, end to end.
evals.expected_output: A read-only answer that names the three entry points and traces POST /refunds from api.py through handlers, validation and service to the store and on to Razorpay with correct references; shows that refunds-bulk writes refunds that skip the order and over-refund checks despite docs/refunds.md and CHANGELOG 0.4.1; explains that the worker retries every OSError, so a timeout after Razorpay accepted a refund sends it again with no idempotency key, contrary to CHANGELOG 0.4.2; that each process holds its own copy of refunds.json; that nothing in the repository records orders; how a refund of exactly Rs 5,000 is handled on each path; and the doc drifts. No file in the repository changes.
expectations: No file in the repository was created, edited or deleted and nothing was committed: `git diff fixture --stat` is empty, `git log fixture..HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty (git-ignored __pycache__ from running the repo's own tests does not count; an untracked notes or planning file does)

It names the three entry points declared in pyproject.toml (refunds-api, refunds-worker, refunds-bulk) and traces POST /refunds from do_POST in src/refunds/api.py through handlers.create_refund, validation.parse and RefundService.create to Store.insert_refund, and every file and line reference given anywhere in the answer points at the code it describes (the grader checks at least three; a wrong file or a line more than five away fails)

It explains that the CSV import in src/refunds/bulk.py writes refunds straight to Store.insert_refund without RefundService, so a bulk refund is never checked against the order existing or against the amount already paid and refunded, and it says this contradicts the claim that bulk follows the same rules (docs/refunds.md line 7 or CHANGELOG.md 0.4.1)
It explains that the worker sends only refunds with status approved and marks a refund sent only after gateway.refund returns, so any OSError leaves it approved and it is sent again on the next poll

It identifies that a timeout or dropped connection (urlopen timeout=10 in gateway.py) after Razorpay has accepted the refund is caught as an OSError and resent on the next poll, and that no idempotency key is sent in the request, so the customer can be refunded twice; and it states that CHANGELOG.md 0.4.2's claim of an idempotency key is not borne out by gateway.py (a crash between the call and set_status alone does not satisfy this)

It explains that the API, the worker and each refunds-bulk run are separate processes that each load refunds.json once into memory (Store.__init__) and rewrite the whole file on every write, and gives a concrete consequence: the worker never sees refunds created after it started, or one process's save erases refunds another process wrote

It states that nothing in the repository records orders or paid amounts (Store.add_order is called only from tests), so the paid amounts the over-refund check reads must be written into the JSON file from outside this repository, and it does not invent where they come from

It reports the doc drifts: `make run` (Makefile line 4) starts the worker, not the API the README says; configuration is read from config.json by src/refunds/config.py, not environment variables (only the Razorpay keys come from the environment, and REFUNDS_DB in .env.example is never read); the approval limit is not read from config.json despite docs/refunds.md and CHANGELOG.md 0.4.1; test files are named *_test.py while CONTRIBUTING.md says test_<module>.py

It gets the boundary at exactly Rs 5,000 (500000 paise) right: through the API such a refund is stored approved (service.py uses >) yet the response carries the needs_manager flag (validation.py uses >= MANAGER_FLAG_FROM), while the same amount through refunds-bulk is held as awaiting_approval (bulk.py uses >=); an answer that says it is held on every path, or does not address the boundary, fails

It does not present anything absent from the repository as fact: no database server, queue, deployment platform, approval screen, authentication layer or idempotency mechanism is described as part of the system
Neither the final message nor any file the run wrote contains an em dash character (checked on the final message in transcript.md, so a run that wrote nothing is still judged)

evals.name: where-to-change-approval-limit
evals.prompt: Where do we decide whether a refund needs manager approval? Finance wants the limit raised from 5,000 to 10,000 rupees next sprint and I want to know everything I'd have to touch before I estimate it. Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A read-only answer listing every place the limit lives and the new value in each place's own unit: MANAGER_APPROVAL_ABOVE in service.py (1,000,000 paise), MANAGER_FLAG_FROM = rupees(5_000) in validation.py (rupees(10_000), since the helper takes rupees), REVIEW_FROM_RUPEES in bulk.py (10000 rupees), and the Rs 5,000 message in handlers.py; the three comparisons that disagree at exactly the limit; the tests that fail and the two that stop exercising the large case; the unused approval_threshold_paise key and the docs and CHANGELOG that say config.json controls it; and refunds already awaiting approval.
expectations: No file in the repository was created, edited or deleted and nothing was committed: `git diff fixture --stat` is empty, `git log fixture..HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty (git-ignored __pycache__ from running the repo's own tests does not count; an untracked notes or planning file does)

It names all four places that must change: MANAGER_APPROVAL_ABOVE = 500_000 with needs_approval in src/refunds/service.py; MANAGER_FLAG_FROM = rupees(5_000) in src/refunds/validation.py, which sets the needs_manager flag; REVIEW_FROM_RUPEES = 5000 in src/refunds/bulk.py, a separate approval decision because the CSV import never calls RefundService; and APPROVAL_NOTE ('Refunds above Rs 5,000 ...') in src/refunds/handlers.py

It gives the correct new value for each place in that place's own unit: 1,000,000 paise (10_00_000) in service.py; rupees(10_000) in validation.py, because rupees() converts whole rupees to paise (an answer that puts 1,000,000 or 1_000_000 into the rupees() call, or tells the reader to use the same paise number there, fails); and 10000 in bulk.py, which counts whole rupees (an explicit rupee-to-paise conversion against one shared paise limit is also accepted for bulk.py)

It points out that the three checks disagree at exactly the limit (service.py uses >, validation.py and bulk.py use >=), so a refund of exactly the limit is auto-approved through the API but held when it comes from the CSV, and it asks or recommends which rule finance wants at exactly Rs 10,000

It names the tests whose assertions would fail (test_threshold_is_exclusive in tests/service_test.py, test_flags_large_refund in tests/validation_test.py, test_rows_become_refunds in tests/bulk_test.py) and works out that two tests stop exercising the large case and need new amounts, not just new assertions: test_large_refund_waits_for_manager uses 600_000 against an order paid 900_000 in setUp, so an amount above 1,000,000 also needs a larger order or it hits OverRefund; and the 7500 rupee row in test_rows_become_refunds becomes approved

It states that approval_threshold_paise in config.json is not read by any code (src/refunds/config.py loads only db_path, port, razorpay_base_url and worker_poll_seconds), so editing config.json alone would change nothing, and that docs/refunds.md (lines 5-6) and CHANGELOG.md 0.4.1 are both wrong in saying the limit comes from config.json

It raises what happens to refunds already stored as awaiting_approval between Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000: the change does not re-evaluate them and nothing in the repository moves a refund out of awaiting_approval
It does not claim the limit is configurable at runtime, or that an approval screen, database or other store exists that the repository does not show
Neither the final message nor any file the run wrote contains an em dash character (checked on the final message in transcript.md, so a run that wrote nothing is still judged)
